concepts.name: PCA Framework: Legal Basis and Regulatory Authority
key_dimensions: RBI's authority to invoke PCA under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Whether PCA is a statutory framework or an administrative/supervisory tool — a common UPSC trap
Distinction between PCA for commercial banks vs. PCA for NBFCs (extended in 2021)
Role of RBI Board vs. RBI Governor in invoking PCA decisions

concepts.name: PCA Trigger Indicators: Capital, Asset Quality, and Leverage
key_dimensions: Three primary risk thresholds: Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR), Net NPA ratio, and Return on Assets (RoA) / Tier-1 Leverage Ratio
Specific numerical thresholds for each indicator (e.g., CRAR below 10.25%, Net NPA above 6%) — exact figures are frequently tested
Why RoA was replaced by Tier-1 Leverage Ratio in the revised 2021 framework
How multiple simultaneous threshold breaches escalate the severity of PCA restrictions

concepts.name: PCA Risk Threshold Levels (Threshold 1, 2, 3): Gradation of Restrictions
key_dimensions: Three-tier gradation system and the specific restrictions imposed at each level
Restrictions at Threshold 1 vs. Threshold 3 — incremental nature of corrective actions
Mandatory vs. discretionary restrictions: which actions RBI must take vs. may take at each level
Common trap: confusing the number of thresholds (3 levels) with the number of indicators (also 3)

concepts.name: Mandatory Restrictions Under PCA
key_dimensions: Prohibition on dividend distribution and capital remittance
Restriction on branch expansion — both domestic and overseas
Cap on management compensation and directors' fees
Prohibition on entering into new lines of business — critical for MCQ distractors

concepts.name: Discretionary Restrictions Under PCA
key_dimensions: Restrictions on credit expansion to specific sectors or borrowers
Reduction in concentration of high-risk assets
Requirement to increase provisioning beyond standard norms
Distinction between discretionary actions and mandatory actions — a key UPSC trap area

concepts.name: PCA and Lending Restrictions: Impact on Credit Flow
key_dimensions: Whether banks under PCA are completely prohibited from lending or only restricted — a common misconception
Specific restriction: banks cannot lend to unrated borrowers or sectors with high risk weighting
Impact of PCA on priority sector lending obligations of affected banks
Systemic risk of simultaneous PCA imposition on multiple banks affecting credit availability

concepts.name: Revised PCA Framework 2021: Key Changes from Original 2017 Framework
key_dimensions: Removal of Return on Assets (RoA) as a trigger; addition of Tier-1 Leverage Ratio
Extension of PCA norms to government-owned banks (which were already covered) vs. new inclusion of small finance banks
Revision of threshold levels and tightening of capital adequacy benchmarks post-Basel III alignment
Why the revision was considered a relaxation in some dimensions vs. tightening in others

concepts.name: PCA Extension to NBFCs (2021): Scope and Applicability
key_dimensions: Which NBFCs are covered: deposit-taking NBFCs, non-deposit-taking systemically important NBFCs, and Core Investment Companies
Which NBFCs are excluded: government NBFCs, primary dealers, housing finance companies under NHB
Trigger indicators for NBFCs vs. scheduled commercial banks — key differences
Significance of including NBFCs after the IL&FS and DHFL crises

concepts.name: PCA vs. RBI's Other Supervisory Interventions: Distinguishing Overlaps
key_dimensions: Distinction between PCA and moratorium under Section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act
PCA vs. Corrective Action Plan (CAP) — supervisory tool vs. structured resolution tool
PCA vs. Resolution Framework (COVID-19 one-time restructuring) — coexistence and conflicts
When RBI escalates from PCA to forced merger or license cancellation — the continuum of intervention

concepts.name: Exit from PCA: Conditions and Process
key_dimensions: Conditions for exit: sustained improvement in all three trigger indicators over at least four quarters
Who decides exit from PCA — RBI's Board for Financial Supervision (BFS) oversight
Instances of banks exiting PCA: UCO Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Maharashtra (2019–2021) — factual recall
Trap: whether a bank can exit PCA on improvement in only one or two indicators (answer: No, all must improve)

concepts.name: PCA and Recapitalization: Interaction with Government's Indradhanush and Recap Bonds
key_dimensions: How government recapitalization (recap bonds) helps banks exit PCA by improving CRAR
Whether recapitalization automatically triggers PCA removal — it does not; RBI assesses independently
Indradhanush framework (2015) vs. PCA framework — complementary or conflicting?
Capital conservation buffer (CCB) under Basel III and its relationship with PCA CRAR thresholds

concepts.name: Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) as a PCA Trigger: Measurement and Classification
key_dimensions: Net NPA ratio (not Gross NPA) used as the PCA trigger — a critical distinction frequently tested
Formula: Net NPA = Gross NPA minus provisions; significance of provisioning in PCA calculus
How Asset Quality Review (AQR) of 2015 led to sudden spike in NPAs and subsequent PCA placements
Relationship between NPA recognition norms (90-day default) and PCA trigger thresholds

concepts.name: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CRAR) as a PCA Trigger: Basel III Linkage
key_dimensions: Minimum CRAR under Basel III: 9% for Indian banks (higher than Basel III's 8%) — India-specific norm
PCA Threshold 1 triggered when CRAR falls below 10.25% (includes Capital Conservation Buffer)
Difference between CRAR, Tier-1 capital ratio, and Common Equity Tier-1 (CET-1) in PCA context
Trap: PCA threshold CRAR is not the same as the minimum regulatory CRAR requirement

concepts.name: PCA and Its Impact on Public Sector Banks: Structural Vulnerability
key_dimensions: Why PSBs are disproportionately represented among PCA banks vs. private banks
Government's dual role as owner (recapitalization) and regulator's independence in imposing PCA
Peak period: 11 PSBs under PCA simultaneously in 2018 — systemic significance
Argument that PCA framework is less effective for PSBs due to implicit government guarantee reducing market discipline

concepts.name: Board for Financial Supervision (BFS): Role in PCA Oversight
key_dimensions: BFS as a committee of RBI's Central Board — its supervisory role over PCA decisions
Composition of BFS: four directors from RBI Central Board plus RBI Governor as Chairman
BFS meets monthly — its frequency and supervisory scope covering banks, NBFCs, and financial institutions
Distinction between BFS's supervisory role and RBI's monetary policy functions — separation of functions

concepts.name: PCA Framework and Financial Stability: Macroprudential Dimensions
key_dimensions: How PCA acts as a macroprudential tool to prevent systemic banking failure
Trade-off between financial stability (PCA restrictions) and credit growth (economic slowdown risk)
IMF/World Bank assessment of India's PCA framework in Financial Sector Assessment Programme (FSAP)
Criticism that PCA is applied too late (reactive) rather than as an early warning preventive tool

concepts.name: PCA and Small Finance Banks / Cooperative Banks: Applicability Boundaries
key_dimensions: Small Finance Banks are covered under the revised PCA framework (2021) — frequently tested inclusion
Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs): covered under amended Banking Regulation Act 2020 — new RBI supervisory jurisdiction
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs): not directly covered under PCA — sponsor bank relationship instead
Payments Banks: excluded from PCA — rationale being their limited lending activity

concepts.name: Prompt Corrective Action: International Comparisons (FDIC's PCA vs. RBI's PCA)
key_dimensions: US origin: FDICIA 1991 introduced PCA in the US following Savings & Loan crisis — historical context
US FDIC's five capital categories vs. India's three threshold levels — structural comparison
Key difference: US PCA is statutory and mandatory; India's PCA is regulatory/supervisory and not backed by a separate statute
Basel Committee's Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision and PCA as a best practice

concepts.name: Governance and Management Reforms Mandated Under PCA
key_dimensions: RBI's power to supersede the board or appoint an administrator under extreme PCA conditions
Fit and proper criteria for bank directors and management tightened under PCA
Requirement for banks to submit a Capital Restoration Plan (CRP) upon entering PCA
Distinction between RBI appointing an administrator (PCA + extreme distress) vs. moratorium (depositor protection focus)

concepts.name: Criticism and Limitations of the PCA Framework
key_dimensions: RBI-Government conflict (2018): government argued PCA was restricting credit flow and hurting MSMEs, sought relaxation
Argument that PCA punishes depositors and borrowers of weak banks rather than their management
Regulatory forbearance risk: delayed recognition of NPAs means banks enter PCA too late for early corrective action
Whether PCA has actually resolved bank stress or merely delayed failures — empirical critique for essay/mains answers
